introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: ANSWER ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: ANSWER ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: ANSWER 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0, Mg = 24.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 $\mathrm{cm^3}$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 $\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,{}^{\circ}C^{-1}}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 273\ \mathrm{K}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Nitrogen and Hydrogen react reversibly as shown by the following reaction.

$\mathrm{N_{2(g)} + 3H_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2NH_{3(g)}}$; $\Delta H = -94$ kJ/mol

(i) State one source of: Hydrogen: ... Nitrogen: ...

(ii) State what would happen to the equilibrium position when: Pressure is increased: ... Temperature is increased: ...

(iii) The yield of ammonia ($\mathrm{NH_3}$) can be increased by withdrawing some ammonia from the equilibrium mixture. Identify and state the principle that accounts for this observation. Principle: ... Statement: ... *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Hydrogen:** natural gas (methane) reacted with steam, $\mathrm{CH_4 + H_2O \rightarrow CO + 3H_2}$ (nickel catalyst, high temperature), or the electrolysis of water. **Nitrogen:** the fractional distillation of liquid air.

(ii) **Pressure increased:** the equilibrium position shifts to the **right**, towards ammonia, because the forward reaction goes from 4 moles of gas (1 + 3) to 2 moles of gas, which reduces the pressure. **Temperature increased:** the equilibrium position shifts to the **left** (towards nitrogen and hydrogen) because the forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H$ is negative) and the system opposes the rise in temperature by absorbing heat; the yield of ammonia falls.

(iii) **Principle:** Le Chatelier's principle.

**Statement:** when a system in equilibrium is subjected to a change in conditions (concentration, pressure or temperature), the position of equilibrium shifts in the direction that opposes (reduces) the change. Removing ammonia lowers its concentration, so the equilibrium shifts to the right to make more ammonia, which increases the yield.

questions.enonce_markdown:
You are given the following reaction:

$\mathrm{CaCO_{3(s)} + 2HCl_{(aq)} \rightarrow CaCl_{2(aq)} + CO_{2(g)} + H_2O_{(l)}}$

(i) State two factors that will affect the rate of this reaction.

(ii) The volume of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas produced is recorded from a graduated syringe. State and explain what could be done to the concentration of HCl in order to obtain more $\mathrm{CO_{2(g)}}$ within a shorter period. Statement: ... Explanation: ... *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Any two of: **concentration of the acid**; **temperature**; **particle size (surface area) of the calcium carbonate** (powder reacts faster than lumps).

(ii) **Statement:** increase the concentration of the hydrochloric acid (use a more concentrated acid).

**Explanation:** a more concentrated acid has more $\mathrm{H^+}$ ions per unit volume, so the acid particles collide with the carbonate more often and more of these collisions are successful. The rate rises, so more $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is collected in a given (shorter) time; if the acid is the limiting reagent, the larger amount of HCl also gives a larger total volume of $\mathrm{CO_2}$.
